atlas.roadmap.branchNote: After Deep Learning, pick a branch
atlas.roadmap.routeResult: Route to {{lesson}}. Lessons on the way: {{count}}. Parts: {{parts}}.
atlas.roadmap.legendNone: No lesson is open yet. Open lessons appear in bold, with a link.
atlas.prereq.none: This lesson needs nothing before it. You can start right away.
atlas.quiz.question: Question {{n}} of {{total}}
atlas.progress.doneStatus: Saved. Press again to unmark it.
atlas.progress.storageBlocked: Your browser is blocking storage. Your progress will be lost when you reload the page.
atlas.runner.editorHint: Tab inserts 4 spaces. Press Esc, then Tab, to leave. Ctrl+Enter runs the code.
atlas.runner.input: Input for input(), one line per read
atlas.runner.firstRunNote: The first run downloads Python, about 10 MB.
atlas.runner.queued: Waiting for another code block to finish…
atlas.runner.longRunning: This code has run for over {{seconds}} seconds. If it is stuck, press Stop.
atlas.runner.stopped: Stopped. You can edit the code and run it again.
atlas.runner.loadFailed: Could not load Python. Check your connection and try again.
atlas.runner.noOutput: The program finished without printing anything.
atlas.runner.outputTruncated: The output is too long, so only the beginning is shown.
atlas.runner.figuresTruncated: Only the first {{count}} figures are shown.
atlas.runner.stdinMissing: The code calls input(), but this block has no input data. On this page, input() cannot ask you.
atlas.runner.hintNameError: Python does not know this name. Check the spelling, or check that the variable is set on an earlier line.
atlas.runner.hintSyntaxError: The statement breaks Python's grammar. Check brackets, colons and quotes on this line or the line above.
atlas.runner.hintIndentationError: The indentation is off. Lines in one block need the same indent, usually 4 spaces.
atlas.runner.hintTypeError: An operation or function got the wrong type, for example a number plus a string.
atlas.runner.hintValueError: The type is right but the value is not, for example array sizes that do not match.
atlas.runner.hintIndexError: The index is past the end of the list or array. Python counts from 0.
atlas.runner.hintKeyError: This key is not in the dict, or this column is not in the table.
atlas.runner.hintAttributeError: This object has no such attribute or method. Check the spelling and the object's type.
atlas.runner.hintModuleNotFoundError: This library is not available on the page. Only numpy, pandas, matplotlib, scipy and scikit-learn are.
atlas.runner.hintEOFError: The code reads input() more times than there are lines in the input box.
atlas.runner.hintGeneric: Read the last line of the error message: it names the error and the reason.
atlas.localCode.sampleNote: From one real run. A model gives a different answer each time.
atlas.vizLinearFit.caption: Drag the two sliders to place a line. Try to find the line with the smallest MSE.
atlas.vizLinearFit.plotLabel: Scatter plot of {{count}} data points, {{y}} against {{x}}, with the line you chose.
atlas.vizLinearFit.residual: Residual: the vertical segment from a point to your line
atlas.vizLinearFit.nearBest: Very close to the best line.
atlas.vizLinearFit.bestNote: No straight line has a smaller MSE than {{mse}}.
atlas.vizLinearFit.meanNote: An X-shaped mark shows the mean point ({{x}}, {{y}}). The best line always passes through it.
atlas.vizPolyFit.caption: Drag the slider to change the degree of the polynomial. It is fitted to the training points only; the test points are kept for scoring.
atlas.vizPolyFit.plotLabel: Scatter plot of {{train}} training points and {{test}} test points, with the degree-{{degree}} polynomial fitted to the training set.
atlas.vizPolyFit.errorLabel: Training and test MSE by polynomial degree, from {{min}} to {{max}}. Chosen degree: {{degree}}.
atlas.vizPolyFit.errorDesc: Training MSE falls from {{trainFirst}} at degree {{min}} to {{trainLast}} at degree {{max}}. Test MSE is smallest at degree {{best}} ({{testBest}}), then rises to {{testLast}} at degree {{max}}.
atlas.vizPolyFit.underfit: Underfitting: the polynomial is too simple; training and test MSE are both high.
atlas.vizPolyFit.goodFit: A good fit: test MSE stays low.
atlas.vizPolyFit.overfit: Overfitting: training MSE is small but test MSE is high; the curve bends to follow the noise.
atlas.vizPolyFit.bestDegree: The degree with the smallest test MSE.
atlas.vizRegularization.caption: Drag the slider to change λ, and press Ridge or Lasso to change the penalty. The polynomial always has degree 15 and is fitted to the training points only.
atlas.vizRegularization.plotLabel: Scatter plot of {{train}} training points and {{test}} test points, with the degree-15 polynomial fitted by {{model}} at λ = {{lambda}}.
atlas.vizRegularization.barsLabel: Bar chart of the 15 coefficients of {{model}} at λ = {{lambda}}: {{zeros}} exactly zero, {{over}} off the chart.
atlas.vizRegularization.barsDesc: Each bar is the coefficient wₖ of the standardized feature xᵏ, for k from 1 to 15. Bars up are positive, bars down are negative.
atlas.vizRegularization.underfit: Underfitting: the penalty is too strong; the coefficients are squeezed towards 0 and both training and test MSE are high.
atlas.vizRegularization.goodFit: A good fit: test MSE stays low.
atlas.vizRegularization.overfit: Overfitting: the penalty is too weak; the coefficients are huge, the curve follows the noise, and test MSE is high.
atlas.vizRegularization.bestLambda: The λ on the slider with the smallest test MSE.
atlas.vizRegularization.announce: {{model}}, λ = {{lambda}}: training MSE {{train}}, test MSE {{test}}, {{zeros}} of {{total}} coefficients are zero. {{zone}}
atlas.vizSampling.caption: Drag the three sliders to change how the next token is chosen, then draw samples. The model’s logits stay the same.
atlas.vizSampling.kept: {{kept}} of {{total}} tokens can still be drawn.
atlas.vizSampling.greedyNote: T = 0: the token with the largest logit is always chosen, which is greedy decoding.
atlas.vizSampling.resetDone: Sliders reset and drawn samples cleared.
atlas.vizGradientDescent.caption: Each step goes against the gradient of the MSE. Pick a learning rate η, then press Step or Run. Floor area is scaled to [0, 1], so the axes are w̃ and b̃. For this data, 2/L ≈ {{limit}}.
atlas.vizGradientDescent.mapLabel: Contour map of the MSE over w̃ and b̃, with the gradient descent path for η = {{eta}} after {{step}} steps.
atlas.vizGradientDescent.mapDesc: The contours are long, tilted ellipses around the bottom ({{w}}, {{b}}), where the MSE is smallest, {{best}}. The path starts at (0, 0), where the MSE is {{start}}.
atlas.vizGradientDescent.controls: Choose the learning rate and run
atlas.vizGradientDescent.chartLabel: MSE by step, on a log scale. After {{step}} steps, the MSE is {{mse}}.
atlas.vizGradientDescent.chartDesc: The dashed line is the smallest MSE, {{best}}. Each mark on the MSE axis is 10 times the one below it.
atlas.vizGradientDescent.hint: Press Step for one step, or Run for up to {{max}} steps.
atlas.vizGradientDescent.reached: At step {{step}}, the MSE is within 1% of the smallest.
atlas.vizGradientDescent.notYet: After {{max}} steps, the MSE is still {{mse}}, not near the bottom yet.
atlas.vizGradientDescent.slowNote: η is small, so every step is short.
atlas.vizGradientDescent.zigzagNote: η is close to 2/L ≈ {{limit}}, so the path jumps back and forth across the valley.
atlas.vizGradientDescent.diverged: Diverging: η is above 2/L ≈ {{limit}}; the MSE grows with every step, and the path leaves the map at step {{step}}.
atlas.vizGradientDescent.atEnd: This is the last step. Press Run to start again.
atlas.vizThreshold.caption: Drag the threshold t. Each dot is one patient; a dot on the line or to its right is predicted ill. The confusion matrix and the four metrics below follow.
atlas.vizThreshold.plotLabel: Axis of the probability of being ill with {{total}} patients: {{pos}} ill, {{neg}} not ill. Threshold line at t = {{t}}, {{predicted}} patients predicted ill.
atlas.vizThreshold.rule: From the line rightwards (p ≥ t): predicted ill
atlas.vizThreshold.matrixLabel: Confusion matrix at t = {{t}}. Rows are the true labels, columns the predictions.
atlas.vizThreshold.noPositive: No positive predictions: precision is 0/0, undefined.
atlas.vizThreshold.announce: t = {{t}}: TP {{tp}}, FP {{fp}}, FN {{fn}}, TN {{tn}}. Accuracy {{accuracy}}, precision {{precision}}, recall {{recall}}, F1 {{f1}}.
atlas.vizGradientFlow.caption: Pick an activation function, an initialization and the number of hidden layers. Each bar is the mean $|\partial\mathcal{L}/\partial\mathbf{z}^{[l]}|$ of one layer, divided by its value at the last layer, on a log scale. The network has {{width}} neurons per layer and runs on {{batch}} random samples; the gradient at the output is fixed.
atlas.vizGradientFlow.chartLabel: Bar chart of the gradient size in {{depth}} hidden layers ({{activation}}, initialization: {{init}}). The gradient at layer 1 is {{ratio}} times the one at the last layer.
atlas.vizGradientFlow.chartDesc: One bar per layer, from layer 1 (next to the input) on the left to the last layer on the right. The last layer is the reference, equal to 1. A bar pointing down: the gradient is smaller than at the last layer; pointing up: larger. Each tick on the vertical axis is ten thousand times the one below.
atlas.vizGradientFlow.gradAxis: Gradient size relative to the last layer (log scale)
atlas.vizGradientFlow.controls: Pick the activation function, the initialization and the number of hidden layers
atlas.vizGradientFlow.ratio: Gradient at layer 1 divided by the last layer
atlas.vizGradientFlow.vanishingNote: the gradient at layer 1 is more than {{limit}} times smaller than at the last layer, so the layers near the input barely learn.
atlas.vizGradientFlow.stableNote: the gradients at layer 1 and at the last layer are within {{limit}} times of each other, so every layer learns.
atlas.vizGradientFlow.explodingNote: the gradient at layer 1 is more than {{limit}} times larger than at the last layer, so the first layers take steps far too large.
atlas.vizGradientFlow.announce: {{activation}}, initialization: {{init}}, {{depth}} hidden layers. The gradient at layer 1 is {{ratio}} times the one at the last layer. {{regime}}.
atlas.vizConvolution.caption: Each cell of the feature map is the sum of 9 products: the 3×3 kernel times the 3×3 window of the image right under it. Pick a kernel, then press a cell of the map (or use the buttons or arrow keys) to move the window. Rows and columns count from 0, as in NumPy.
atlas.vizConvolution.imageLabel: 8×8 greyscale image. The 3×3 window covers rows {{r0}} to {{r1}}, columns {{c0}} to {{c1}}.
atlas.vizConvolution.imageDesc: The background is 0. In the middle is a bright 4×4 square of 9s, rows 2 to 5 and columns 2 to 5.
atlas.vizConvolution.productsTitle: Window times kernel, cell by cell
atlas.vizConvolution.legend: Brown cell: positive. Blue cell: negative. The stronger the colour, the further from 0.
atlas.vizConvolution.identityNote: Identity: only the middle weight is 1, so the map copies the middle 6×6 of the image exactly.
atlas.vizConvolution.blurNote: Blur: each cell is the mean of 9 pixels, so the sharp edge of the square fades from 9 down to 1.
atlas.vizConvolution.sharpenNote: Sharpen: the middle pixel times 5, minus its four neighbours, so the numbers jump up along the edge of the square (18, 27) and turn negative just outside it (−9).
atlas.vizConvolution.sobelVerticalNote: Vertical Sobel: positive on the left edge of the square (dark to bright going right), negative on the right edge, 0 on flat areas.
atlas.vizConvolution.sobelHorizontalNote: Horizontal Sobel: positive on the top edge of the square (dark to bright going down), negative on the bottom edge, 0 on flat areas.
atlas.vizBpeMerge.caption: BPE runs step by step on the 7 syllables of the Theory section. Each time you press Next step, the adjacent pair of symbols with the largest count is merged into one new symbol.
atlas.vizBpeMerge.controls: Run one merge at a time
atlas.vizBpeMerge.pairsStart: Counts of adjacent pairs at the start
atlas.vizBpeMerge.syllablesLabel: How each syllable is split. The piece made at this step is filled and bold.
atlas.vizBpeMerge.startNote: Step 0: each syllable is a sequence of characters, with _ at the end. The vocabulary has {{size}} symbols.
atlas.vizBpeMerge.tieNote: {{n}} pairs share the count {{count}}: the pair met first wins, reading the syllables from top to bottom, each from left to right.
atlas.vizBpeMerge.announceStep: Step {{step}}: merge {{a}} + {{b}} into {{ab}}, count {{count}}. The vocabulary has {{size}} tokens.
atlas.vizBpeMerge.announceEnd: All {{total}} merges done. Press Reset to run again from the start.
atlas.vizDiffusion.caption: Drag the slider to change the step t. The clean image and the noise stay the same; only the two coefficients change: the image part shrinks, the noise part grows.
atlas.vizDiffusion.noiseLabel: Fixed 16 × 16 noise: each cell a random number from a normal distribution.
atlas.vizDiffusion.xtLabel: Noisy image at step t = {{t}}: {{signal}} times the clean image plus {{noise}} times the noise.
atlas.vizDiffusion.shadeKey: A cell the colour of the background is −1, a cell the colour of the text is 1; values outside [−1, 1] show as the nearer end.
atlas.vizDiffusion.chartLabel: Chart of the two coefficients over the step t from 0 to {{T}}, with a vertical line at t = {{t}}.
atlas.vizDiffusion.chartDesc: The image coefficient goes from 1 down to almost 0, the noise coefficient from 0 up to almost 1. The two lines cross at about t = {{cross}}.
atlas.vizDiffusion.startNote: t = 0: no noise yet, the noisy image is the clean image.
atlas.vizDiffusion.midNote: The squares of the two coefficients always add up to 1: what the image loses, the noise makes up.
atlas.vizDiffusion.endNote: Image coefficient below {{limit}}: almost pure noise.
